status: Frozen before numerical execution; all resource cells will be reported
purpose: Determine whether observation-window or future-noise resources relieve the previously saved prediction ambiguity
scope: Conditional synthetic resource diagnosis, not a new design algorithm or external validation
reuse: The same 16 observed pilots, four spectra, known G(0)=1, rate support and two target functions; no new pilot replication claim
confirmation_plan: Fixed ramp_hold and fixed cycle, 32 samples each at linspace(0.25,T,32); no outcome-dependent schedule selection
cost: 80 response observations in three runs; summed observation-window duration 8+2*T, not equal time or equal instrumentation cost
future_noise: Exactly known uniform amplitude; common standard uniform vector within each pilot case, scaled by amplitude across resource cells; disjoint from original pilot stream
score: max(G20 worst conditional diameter/0.2, heldout_sigma20 worst conditional diameter/0.1)

resource_gate.requirement: For a reported resource cell, its group-mean outer score is <=0.8 times the original fixed-baseline group-mean inner score for at least two truth groups including continuous_uniform, and every slow_three pilot has outer score <=1
resource_gate.interpretation: This diagnoses physical information headroom with changed resources. It does not reverse the failed equal-resource loading-library gate or establish innovation.

validation: T=8, future amplitude=0.01 reproduces the previous fixed-cycle inner and outer bounds
Each outer bracket exceeds the inner bracket and contains the realized posterior widths
All simulated supported targets are contained in realized outer intervals
Every saved LP primal/dual witness is replayed without optimization
At fixed sampling horizon, worst conditional diameters cannot increase when future noise decreases
No monotonicity is assumed across horizons because a stretched sampling schedule is not nested
Track old finite-spectrum pair survival and reoptimize fresh pairs; removal of old pairs alone does not prove identification
limitations: Known support, normalization and exact bounded noise; no calibration or model-validation claim
Only four development pilots per truth; no population confidence or blind-test inference
Smaller noise is a hypothetical instrument resource, not a demonstrated attainable precision
Floating-point LP dual checks are not outward-rounded continuum certificates
No comparison against an adaptive algorithm and no new-method superiority claim
